summary: Landable. DELTA VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by reading: `git diff --cached -- . ':(exclude)baselines/review.txt' | sha256sum` returns 7cadde4311554511eb898e9b58c5e16654f73bfabd54740c1c9c31ee32580a56 exactly -- the hash I passed at round 3 -- so every one of the eight other staged paths is byte-identical and the whole delta is the single added `rounds:M0.79` line in baselines/review.txt. `git diff --cached --stat` shows 9 files, 132 insertions, 0 deletions, no ADR and no code. Still no test file in the staged set. THE ARGUMENT IS ACCURATE WHERE IT TOUCHES MY LANE, checked against the recorded verdicts rather than from memory. (1) The scope contradiction: r1 F1 (reviewer, major) and my r1 M0.79-T2 both located frontmatter line 3 'Use when writing any reply, review report or finding' against a body out-of-scope clause reading 'written for other people, or persist beyond the conversation ... Documentation, READMEs, reports, published artifacts'; a verdict satisfies both limbs, and .harness/review/<sha>.<role>.json is where it persists. 'The reviewers pointed at the skill landed in the section telling them to write at natural length' is F1's own sentence and is correct. (2) Never-cut protecting a number but not provenance: my r1 M0.79-T1 and r1 F2, same defect from both roles; 'non-negotiable 4 degraded by a style rule rather than by a bad reviewer' is T1's wording. Both are recorded in past tense about the pre-fix bytes, so neither is a present-tense claim about a state that no longer exists. The three collateral claims I could check are true: the packet for this round does select standards from paths and lists git/sdd/testing/performance with no cost.md; scripts/build-index.sh:32 globs '.agents/skills/*/' from the WORKTREE, so 'reads the WORKTREE so it blocked every commit' is a fact about the script, not an inference; check-reviewed.sh:195 keys the waiver on `rounds:M0.79`, which is what the added line uses. ON 'TWICE', STATED AS INFERENCE BECAUSE I COULD NOT MEASURE IT: only ONE recorded round carries ADR-0036 -- staged trees 73bbbb56 (r1) and b18857410502 (r3) have no 0036 under docs/internal/product/decisions/, 469567ea (r2) does. The second sweep left no verdict. It is consistent with an orphan .harness/review/77b8605b....gates written at 07:19 with no verdict beside it, between r2's records and 7cadde43's, and with both r3 verdicts having gone out of their way to check the index for 0036. I neither confirm nor refute the count; I raise no finding on it, because I have no evidence against it. MY THREE MINORS STILL STAND UNCHANGED, carried forward below so the landing hash carries them: the bytes they cite are the same bytes. That they are recorded in the commit body I CANNOT verify -- .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG still holds M4.10's message and the body is not in the staged bytes or under the hash. Recording rather than fixing is what I recommended and I still recommend it: the fix surface would be new prose in the file that governs reviewer output. And I confirm again, for these bytes, that .agents/skills/brevity/SKILL.md governs my output without weakening it -- review/SKILL.md:130-135 and .claude/agents/test-reviewer.md:52-67 keep file:line, severity, the failure scenario and the surviving mutation, and this verdict is written at the length the evidence needs.

findings.summary: The provenance paragraph corrects the abbreviation claim 30 lines below it, under an unrelated heading, leaving the false sentence in place at the point of use.
findings.failure_scenario: Line 52 reads 'No invented abbreviations (cfg, impl, req, res, fn, auth). The tokenizer splits them the same as the full word: zero tokens saved'. Lines 81-85 say the opposite about the same example: '"auth" is one token where "authentication" is several, so that abbreviation does save tokens'. The correction sits under '## Write at full length when', two headings past '## Never fake-compress', so an agent that reads the Never-fake-compress section and applies it never reaches the contradiction. The file is loaded for output style, not read end to end. Answering the question put to me directly: this is better than deletion in that it keeps the readability ground the rules actually stand on, and worse than deletion in that a reader at line 52 still gets a sentence the same file later calls false -- the strictly better third option was to delete the tokenizer justification from line 52 and keep the readability clause that follows it ('the reader still decodes; the full word is cheaper and clearer'), which loses nothing the provenance paragraph says is load-bearing. No gate covers a document contradicting itself. Minor because it is in the fake-compress list, not the Never-cut list: no evidence in a finding is at risk, so it does not touch review quality, which is my lane. Fixing it costs another round and the packet says that is usually wrong.

findings.summary: A line-number self-citation in a mutable file; the repository's own gate table records that a number goes stale silently.
findings.failure_scenario: Line 82 reads 'here because line 43 of this file demands exactly that'. Line 43 today is 'Whether a result was MEASURED or inferred', so it resolves as staged -- I checked. Insert one bullet anywhere above it, which the Never-cut list is exactly the kind of list that grows, and the citation silently repoints at line 43's new occupant ('Negations: not, never, no...'), making the provenance paragraph cite a rule that does not demand what it claims. Nothing catches it: check-links.sh resolves markdown links, not line numbers, and check-rule-citations.sh is scoped to review.md's rule NAMES -- its own entry in the AGENTS.md gate table exists because 'a number goes stale silently'. AGENTS.md's Never list states the same rule for task IDs. Fix is to cite the rule by its text ('the Never-cut rule on MEASURED versus inferred') rather than by ordinal. Minor: a stale pointer degrades the explanation, not the finding format.

findings.summary: The briefs' protected-set enumerations read as exhaustive and are subsets of the mirror's five; a closed grammar around a shorter list is the mechanism that drops an item.
findings.failure_scenario: Answering the question put to me: do NOT align the briefs to the mirror's five. Three verbatim copies of one list is the fork skills/README.md rule 5 forbids, and the three lists disagreeing is what produced round 2's mirror finding in the first place; review/SKILL.md:130-135 is now the single authority and brevity/SKILL.md:40-46 independently protects negations, measured-versus-inferred and decision-changing caveats for any consumer, so the omission is not a hole. What IS a defect is the grammar, not the length: reviewer.md:36-38 says 'It never overrides the finding format -- file:line, a severity, and the concrete failure scenario stay, in full', which reads closed. The concrete failure: a production reviewer under brevity pressure reads that enumeration, does not find 'whether a result was measured or inferred' in it, treats the omission as permission, and writes 'the mutation survives' where it meant 'by inspection, the mutation survives' -- the exact F2 failure that brevity/SKILL.md:43-45 was added to close, now reachable through the brief rather than through the skill. test-reviewer.md:62-64 has the same closed grammar over four items. The fix is one word ('at least these stay'), or a pointer to the mirror instead of a restatement -- not a third copy of the list. Minor: both briefs already link the skill, so the protection is reachable; and the packet is explicit that fixing a minor is usually wrong because the next round's surface is the prose the fix adds.
